title: A Girls Trip to Kenya, Planned Around the Mara, the Coast and One Good Night in Nairobi
meta_title: Girls Trip to Kenya: Mara, Diani and Nairobi Nights
meta_description: Plan a girls trip to Kenya: a 9-day Mara, Diani and Nairobi route, vehicles and rooming for friends, real cost drivers and safety tips.
excerpt: A girls trip to Kenya works best as safari, beach and Nairobi in one private plan. Here is the route, the rooming and vehicle set-up, and what drives the cost.
content:
A girls trip to Kenya works best as three short chapters: two or three nights on safari in the Masai Mara (or Amboseli plus the Mara), four nights on the beach at Diani, and one or two evenings in Nairobi at either end. Eight to ten days covers it comfortably, with a private vehicle for your group.

The hard part of a girls trip to Kenya is rarely Kenya itself. It is getting five or eight friends with different budgets, leave allowances and ideas of a good holiday to agree on one plan. This guide gives the organiser a route, a rooming and vehicle plan, an honest view of where the money goes, and the safety points worth sharing in the group chat before anyone books a flight.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 8-10 days (safari, beach and a night or two in Nairobi)
  • Group size per vehicle: up to 6 friends in one pop-up roof 4x4, so everyone has a window seat
  • Masai Mara reserve fee: US$100 per adult per day January-June, US$200 July-December (checked November 2026)
  • Nairobi to Diani: about 1 hour 10 minutes by light aircraft from Wilson Airport (checked November 2026)
  • Luggage on safari flights: 15kg per person in soft bags on most routes, 20kg on Diani flights (checked November 2026)
  • Entry: Kenya eTA for most visitors, applied for online at least 2 weeks before travel

What Does a Girls Trip to Kenya Usually Look Like?

A girls trip to Kenya usually pairs a big-game safari with time on the Indian Ocean coast, bookended by Nairobi. The safari gives the stories, the beach gives the rest, and Nairobi gives the restaurants, the Giraffe Centre and a proper night out together.

Most girls trip to Kenya requests we plan fall into one of three shapes. The classic girls trip to Kenya is safari first, beach second, so the dusty early starts come before the cocktails and nobody flies home exhausted. The celebration version adds one standout moment, such as a hot air balloon over the Mara at sunrise or a private bush dinner on a birthday night. The short-leave version, for friends who can only take a week, skips the road and flies everywhere.

What makes a girls trip to Kenya different from a standard safari is the pacing. You want space for long lunches, a spa afternoon, an evening where half the group goes out and half stays in, and room for one friend to lie by the pool while the others go on a walking safari. A private itinerary lets you build those gaps in; a shared tour with strangers does not.

How Many Days Do You Need for Safari, Beach and Nairobi?

Nine days is the sweet spot for most friend groups: one night in Nairobi, three nights on safari, four on the coast and a final evening back in Nairobi or a direct flight home from Mombasa. Seven days works if you fly between every stop; twelve lets you add Amboseli or Lake Naivasha.

The table below is a sample nine-day girls trip to Kenya that we often use as a starting point. Every day can be swapped, shortened or upgraded.

DayWhereWhat the group does
1NairobiArrive, transfer to a garden hotel in Karen or Westlands, welcome dinner
2Nairobi to Masai MaraGiraffe Centre in the morning, then a 45-minute flight from Wilson Airport (or about 5 hours by road), afternoon game drive
3Masai MaraFull-day game drive with a bush picnic, or an optional sunrise balloon flight
4Masai MaraMorning drive, Maasai village visit or a lazy afternoon at camp, sundowners
5Mara to DianiLight aircraft to the coast via Nairobi, check in to a beach hotel
6-8Diani BeachBeach days, a dhow trip, snorkelling, spa time, one dressed-up dinner
9Diani to NairobiFly back for an evening flight home, or a last night out in the city

If your group would rather see two parks, our fly-in safari from Diani to Amboseli and the Masai Mara starts and ends on the coast, so you can do the beach first and slot the safari into the middle of the trip. For a road-based version through Amboseli, Lake Nakuru and the Mara, the 6-day Amboseli and Masai Mara safari is a good base to customise.

Which Kenya Parks Suit a Group of Friends?

The Masai Mara suits almost every group of friends because it delivers big cats quickly and has camps at every price level. Amboseli adds elephants under Kilimanjaro, and Lake Naivasha is the easy, relaxed stop for groups who want boat rides and walking rather than more long drives.

Masai Mara: the headline act

The Mara is where most first-timers see lions, cheetahs and, from about July to October, the wildebeest migration. For a girls trip to Kenya, three nights is ideal and two is the minimum. Staying in a private conservancy on the edge of the reserve gives you night drives, walking safaris and far fewer vehicles at each sighting, which a group celebrating something special tends to love. Our guide to the best time to visit the Masai Mara explains how each month changes the experience.

Amboseli: the photo stop

Amboseli National Park is about 4 hours by road from Nairobi and is known for large elephant herds with Kilimanjaro on the skyline on clear mornings. It works as a two-night add-on before the Mara on a longer girls trip to Kenya, and its open, flat plains make it easy for everyone in the vehicle to get the same shot.

Lake Naivasha: the slow afternoon

Naivasha breaks up the drive between Nairobi and the Mara with a boat ride among hippos, a walk on Crescent Island and lakeside lodges with gardens. It is a gentle stop for a group that includes a friend who is nervous about long game drives.

Vehicles, Rooms and Splitting the Bill Fairly

A private group needs one pop-up roof 4x4 for every six friends, rooms planned before deposits are paid, and a clear rule for who pays for what. Settling these three things early prevents most of the arguments that spoil group holidays.

Vehicles and window seats

Kenya's safari Land Cruisers usually seat six or seven guests, but a group of seven in one vehicle means someone loses a window seat and a clear view through the roof hatch. For a girls trip to Kenya with seven to twelve friends, we recommend two vehicles with their own guides. That also lets one vehicle head out at dawn for photographers while the other leaves after breakfast.

Rooming without the awkward conversation

On a girls trip to Kenya, rooming matters. Most safari camps have twin and double tents, a few have triples, and family tents with two bedrooms are perfect for four friends who want to share a deck. Single rooms often carry a supplement, so ask everyone early whether they want to share. If your numbers are odd, a family tent or a triple can save the solo friend from paying extra.

Splitting costs on a girls trip to Kenya

The fairest approach is one shared core (vehicle, guide, park fees, accommodation and flights) split evenly, with optional extras paid individually. A hot air balloon flight over the Mara, for example, is listed at USD 500 per person on our trip pages, so not everyone will want it. A single invoice for the core and separate bookings for extras keeps the group chat calm.

How Much Does a Girls Trip to Kenya Cost?

A girls trip to Kenya costs most during the July-December high season, when the Mara reserve fee doubles to US$200 per adult per day. Your accommodation tier, the number of vehicles, flying versus driving and the beach hotel make the biggest differences, so every quote is built around your group.

Group size helps on a girls trip to Kenya. A vehicle and guide cost the same whether three or six friends use them, so the per-person share falls as seats fill. The table shows how each choice moves the price, without inventing package figures.

Cost driverLower-cost choiceHigher-cost choice
SeasonJanuary-June (Mara fee US$100 per day)July-December (Mara fee US$200 per day)
Getting aroundRoad safari in a private 4x4Light aircraft between every stop
Safari stayReserve-side lodge or tented campConservancy camp with walks and night drives
RoomsFriends sharing twins, triples or family tentsSingle rooms with supplements
ExtrasVillage visit, sundowners, beach daysBalloon flight (USD 500 per person), private dinners

Park fees are set by the authorities, not by us, and they change. Check our Kenya park fees guide and confirm the latest figures before you book. The Mara rates above are published by Narok County, which runs the reserve.

Nairobi Nights and Diani Days: Getting the Balance Right

Nairobi and Diani give a girls trip to Kenya its social side. In Nairobi, plan one daytime outing and one good dinner; on the coast, plan almost nothing and let the group set the pace. Both work best with transfers booked in advance rather than hailing rides late at night.

What should you do in Nairobi with a group?

On a girls trip to Kenya, Nairobi deserves more than an airport stop. Feed giraffes at the Giraffe Centre in Langata, visit the elephant orphanage at feeding time, browse a craft market, then book a table at one of the city's restaurants in Karen or Westlands. Our guide to the elephant orphanage and Giraffe Centre has timings, and the day trips from Nairobi post covers Hell's Gate, Lake Naivasha and Nairobi National Park if you have a spare day.

Diani: why the coast works for friends

Diani Beach, south of Mombasa, has a long stretch of white sand, warm water and plenty of hotels with pools and spas. A dhow trip to the Kisite marine area, snorkelling, a beach massage and one dressed-up dinner is about the right amount of activity for most groups after the safari half of a girls trip to Kenya.

Safarilink flies from Wilson Airport to Diani in about 1 hour 10 minutes, with a 20kg baggage allowance on that route compared with 15kg on most safari routes (checked November 2026 on the Safarilink baggage page). Pack the beach outfits in a soft bag that fits the lower safari limit and you will not have to leave anything behind in Nairobi. If the coast is the main event for your group, our bush and beach safaris are built around exactly this split.

Is Kenya Safe for a Group of Women Travelling Together?

A girls trip to Kenya is a well-trodden route for groups of women, and a private safari with a guide, pre-booked transfers and vetted lodges removes most of the common risks. The precautions that matter are the ones you would take in any big city: watch your drinks, avoid walking alone at night and use trusted transport.

The UK government's Kenya travel advice (updated November 2026) warns against accepting drinks from strangers in bars and clubs because of spiking, advises not walking alone in isolated areas even in daylight, and suggests dressing conservatively away from resorts, particularly in Mombasa. It also notes that criminals use dating apps to target visitors, and that crime tends to rise around Christmas and New Year. Our full Kenya safety guide covers the safari side in more detail.

On the safari part of a girls trip to Kenya, safety is mostly about following your guide: stay in the vehicle unless told otherwise, and let camp staff walk you to your tent after dark. Entry is straightforward too: most nationalities need a Kenya eTA, and the local authorities recommend applying at least two weeks before departure, with a passport valid for six months and two blank pages. Our Kenya eTA guide walks through the application.

Insider Tips

  • Name one organiser: one person talks to us and shares updates, which keeps quotes and decisions moving
  • Agree the budget before the dates: it decides the season, the camps and whether you fly or drive
  • Collect passport details early: eTA applications need them, and light aircraft bookings need exact names
  • Pack neutral safari clothes: khaki, olive and beige for game drives; save the bright colours for Diani
  • Plan one surprise: a bush breakfast, a cake at camp or a sunset dhow is easy to arrange quietly through us
  • Leave a free afternoon: groups that rest together argue less and enjoy the big moments more

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days do you need for a girls trip to Kenya?

A girls trip to Kenya needs about nine days to include a proper safari and beach time: one night in Nairobi, three nights in the Masai Mara and four nights at Diani, plus travel days. Seven days is possible if you fly between stops, and ten to twelve days lets you add Amboseli or Lake Naivasha without rushing.

What is the best month for a girls trip to Kenya?

The best months depend on what the group wants most. July to October brings the wildebeest migration to the Masai Mara but the highest park fees and prices. January to March is dry, warm and better value, which suits groups on a tighter budget. Many groups avoid April and May, when the long rains usually fall.

Can we have our own private safari vehicle as a group of friends?

Yes. Divulge Adventures plans every group trip with private vehicles, so your friends never share with strangers. One pop-up roof 4x4 comfortably takes up to six people with a window seat each. Groups of seven to twelve usually travel in two vehicles, each with its own guide, which also allows different start times.

Is Diani or Zanzibar better after a Kenya safari?

Diani is the simpler choice after a Kenya safari because it is a domestic flight of about 1 hour 10 minutes from Nairobi's Wilson Airport, with no border crossing. Zanzibar suits groups who want Stone Town's history and are happy to add an international hop and Tanzania's entry rules to the plan.

Do we need a visa for Kenya?

Most visitors need a Kenya eTA rather than a traditional visa, applied for online before travel. The authorities recommend applying at least two weeks ahead, and passports need six months' validity and two blank pages. Collect everyone's passport details early so the organiser can check each application has gone through before flights are paid.

Final Thoughts

A girls trip to Kenya comes together in three parts: a private safari with a window seat for everyone, a beach stay long enough to rest, and a Nairobi night to celebrate.
